t:
Section 2867 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1997 (division B of Public Law 104–201; 110 Stat. 2806), as amended by section 8135(a) of the Department of Defense Appropriations Act, 1997 (section 101(b) of division A of the Omnibus Consolidated Appropriations Act, 1997 (Public Law 104–208; 110 Stat. 3009–118)), and as amended by section 2862 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 (division B of Public Law 112–81; 125 Stat. 1701), is further amended—
    (1) by striking “Mike O’Callaghan Federal Medical Center” each place it appears and inserting “Mike O’Callaghan Military Medical Center”; and 
    (2) in the heading, by striking “mike o’callaghan” and all that follows and inserting “mike o’callaghan military medical center.”.

fable.w: This section is a technical amendment that renames a medical facility in an earlier statute. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: by striking “Mike O’Callaghan Federal Medical Center” each place it appears and inserting “Mike O’Callaghan Military Medical Center”

opus.w: This section is a technical amendment that renames a facility in an existing statute. It sets up no process for states, experts, the public or any other outside party to be consulted on a federal decision. It also grants no right to object or sue. Any reading that finds participation here would rest only on the procedural setting of an authorization act, not on any outside-party involvement.
opus.s: by striking “Mike O’Callaghan Federal Medical Center” each place it appears and inserting “Mike O’Callaghan Military Medical Center”
opus.b: The tempting reading is to see a medical center named under a military construction act as some kind of federal decision. But the section only changes a name in an existing statute. Nobody outside the federal government is involved, and there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to the statute to change the name of a military medical center. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. The action is purely legislative and administrative within the government.
qwen_chat.s: by striking “Mike O’Callaghan Federal Medical Center” each place it appears and inserting “Mike O’Callaghan Military Medical Center”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that renaming a facility involves public input or consultation, but the text itself contains no such requirement. It is purely a legislative amendment to correct a name in the statute.
